produced_findings.claim: Off-by-one in `page()` returns an extra item on every page The line `end = offset + page_size + 1` gives a slice of `offset` up to `offset + page_size + 1`, which is `page_size + 1` elements. For `items=[1..10]`, `page_number=1`, `page_size=3`, the offset is 0 and the result is `[1, 2, 3, 4]` instead of `[1, 2, 3]`. Page 2 returns `[4, 5, 6, 7]`, so item 4 appears on both pages. The committed version used `offset + page_size`, which was correct. Every page overlaps the next by one item, and callers get more rows than `page_size`. Consumers will see duplicated items across pages and may break contracts that assume at most `page_size` items. Any caller that detects the last page by comparing the result length to `page_size` will behave wrongly.
